title: Disrespect Between Colleagues Can Derail the Team
author: Admired Leadership
summary: This piece argues that while respect is essential for high-performing teams, it's actually the presence or absence of disrespect that best predicts team performance. The author distinguishes two sources of disrespect -- character and competence -- and notes that the disrespected party isn't always aware the contempt exists, even though its effects ripple through team dynamics regardless. The recommended remedy is a two-step process: set an explicit no-exceptions standard for respectful behavior, then address contempt privately by helping the resentful team member find and focus on the disrespected colleague's genuine value. Left unaddressed, the piece warns, disrespect functions like a cancer that quietly undermines everything a team is trying to accomplish.
points: Disrespect, more than the presence of respect, is the strongest predictor of team performance.
Disrespect typically stems from questions of character or competence, sometimes unknown to the disrespected party.
Leaders should set an explicit, no-exceptions standard for respectful behavior on the team.
Addressing contempt privately, by highlighting the disrespected colleague's value, is the recommended remedy.
quotes: But as important as respect is for team success, it is how leaders manage disrespect that has the largest influence on team performance.
Disrespect in a team can fester over time and spoil everything a team tries to do.
Contempt between even two team members changes the team conversation, thereby undermining the dynamic of a team.
The first step is to make sure the team operates from a set of rules that includes respectful behavior from everyone. There can be no exceptions to this standard.
Disrespect between team members is a cancer that eats away at the positive climate all teams need to succeed.
